title: Smoky Beef Chilli
description: A dark, thick chilli with properly browned mince, smoked paprika and a spoonful of cocoa for depth. It needs time rather than effort, and tastes even better reheated.

steps.text: Heat half the oil in a large casserole over a high heat. Add half the mince, press it into a flat layer and leave it without stirring until the underside is dark brown. Break it up, cook for a couple of minutes more, then tip into a bowl. Repeat with the remaining mince, without adding more oil.
steps.tip: Grey, steamed mince makes a flat-tasting chilli. Let it get genuinely brown and a bit crusty.

steps.text: Turn the heat down to medium and add the remaining oil, the onions and the peppers with a pinch of salt. Cook, scraping up the browned bits, until soft.
Add the garlic, smoked paprika, cumin, chilli powder, oregano and cinnamon and stir for a minute. Add the tomato puree and cook, stirring, for a minute more.
Return the mince to the pan. Add the chopped tomatoes, stock, cocoa and salt and stir well. Bring to the boil, then turn the heat down low, part-cover with the lid and simmer, stirring occasionally.

Stir in the kidney beans and simmer with the lid off until the chilli is thick and glossy and a spoon dragged across the base leaves a trail. Meanwhile, cook the rice following the packet instructions.
Take the chilli off the heat, stir in the lime juice and leave it to stand. Taste and adjust the salt and heat.
Serve over the rice with the coriander scattered on top.

tips: Start with 1 tsp of chilli powder if you are feeding children, and put hot sauce on the table for everyone else.
Make it a day ahead if you can. The flavours round out overnight in the fridge.

substitutions.note: use 20g, and check it is dairy-free if that matters

substitutions.use: pork mince or a half-and-half mix

storage: Keeps for 4 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer, without the rice. Defrost fully and reheat until piping hot.
author: Simmer
